dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3701.text: A mallet with a transverse head; west of the passes it is called 㯢. Formed from 木, with 灷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3702.text: A ritual grain vessel, 瑚槤. Formed from 木, with 連 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3703.text: Something used to support vessels. Formed from 木, with 廣 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a curtain or screen.

shuowen:3704.text: Something used to lift food. Formed from 木, with 具 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3705.text: The wooden piece at the end of a well rope. Formed from 木, with 毄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3706.text: A silk-winding frame. Formed from 木, with 爾 indicating the sound. Read like 柅.

shuowen:3707.text: The part that controls release is called 機. Formed from 木, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3708.text: The part of a loom holding the warp. Formed from 木, with 朕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3709.text: The part of a loom holding the weft. Formed from 木, with 予 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3710.text: The part of a loom holding the woven silk. Formed from 木, with 复 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3711.text: A shoe last. Formed from 木, with 爰 indicating the sound. Read like 撝 in 指撝.

shuowen:3712.text: A bark box made by the Man and Yi peoples, shaped like a covered wine vessel. Formed from 木, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3713.text: A platform, 棧. Formed from 木, with 朋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3714.text: A platform, 棚. A cart of bamboo and wood is called 棧. Formed from 木, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3715.text: To enclose with brushwood and timber. Formed from 木, with 存 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3716.text: The bottom of a basket. Formed from 木, with 國 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3717.text: Wooden steps or a ladder. Formed from 木, with 弟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3718.text: A staff. Formed from 木, with 長 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a standard or model.

shuowen:3719.text: A ring through an ox’s nose. Formed from 木, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3720.text: A whip. Formed from 木, with 耑 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to measure out, 椯度. Another: to cut away.

shuowen:3721.text: A stake. Formed from 木, with 厥 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a door peg or threshold.

shuowen:3722.text: A stake. Formed from 木, with 戠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3723.text: To hold or support. Formed from 木, with 丈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3724.text: A club, 棓. Formed from 木, with 犮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3725.text: A wooden club, 棁. Formed from 木, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3726.text: To strike. In Qi it is called 終葵. Formed from 木, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3727.text: An axe handle. Formed from 木, with 可 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3728.text: A wooden staff. Formed from 木, with 兌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3729.text: An axe handle, 柯. Formed from 木, with 丙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3730.text: A 欑 staff. Formed from 木, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3731.text: A staff of bundled bamboo. Formed from 木, with 贊 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to pierce. Another: clustered trees.

shuowen:3732.text: The handle of a silk-winding reel. Formed from 木, with 尸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3733.text: Something used to brace bows and crossbows. Formed from 木, with 㫄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3734.text: A bow brace, 㮄. Formed from 木, with 敬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3735.text: An arrow notch, 栝. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 隱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3736.text: An arrow notch, 𨽌. Formed from 木, with 𠯑 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the notch of an arrow, where it meets the string.

shuowen:3737.text: A board-game piece. Formed from 木, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3738.text: To join or graft wood. Formed from 木, with 妾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3739.text: 栙雙; the object denoted is uncertain. Formed from 木, with 夅 indicating the sound. Read like 鴻.

shuowen:3740.text: Wood for heating a stove. Formed from 木, with 舌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3741.text: A feeding vessel for livestock and beasts. Formed from 木, with 曹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3742.text: An aiming mark for shooting. Formed from 木 and 自. Li Yangbing says: “自 does not indicate the sound; it is abbreviated 劓.”

shuowen:3743.text: A square wooden vessel holding six sheng. Formed from 木, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3744.text: A large shield. Formed from 木, with 魯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3745.text: The collective name for the five notes and eight instrumental timbres. Depicts large and small drums; 木 represents their stand.

shuowen:3746.text: The feet of a railing. Formed from 木, with 付 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3747.text: A stick for striking a drum. Formed from 木, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3748.text: The musical instrument 柷. Formed from 木, with 空 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3749.text: A musical instrument, hollow wood, used to stop the sound and mark its divisions. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 祝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3750.text: An unworked writing tablet. Formed from 木, with 斬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3751.text: A writing slip. Formed from 木, with 乙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3752.text: A written seal or endorsement. Formed from 木, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3753.text: A written document two chi long. Formed from 木, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3754.text: A travel pass or credential. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 啟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3755.text: The patterned bindings wound around a cart shaft. Formed from 木, with 敄 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Five bindings on the arched shaft.”

shuowen:3756.text: A portable barrier. Formed from 木, with 互 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Set up two layers of 梐枑 barriers.”

shuowen:3757.text: The 梐枑 barrier. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 陛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3758.text: A load-bearing frame on a donkey’s back. Formed from 木, with 及 indicating the sound. Also read like 急.

shuowen:3759.text: A donkey’s carrying frame, 极. Formed from 木, with 去 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3760.text: The yoke of a large cart. Formed from 木, with 鬲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3761.text: The hollow inside a wheel hub. Formed from 木, with 喿 indicating the sound. Read like 藪.

shuowen:3762.text: A vessel for holding grease. Formed from 木, with 咼 indicating the sound. Read like 過.

shuowen:3763.text: A horse-tethering post. Formed from 木, with 卬 indicating the sound. Another explanation: firm.

shuowen:3764.text: 棝斗, a device for shooting rats. Formed from 木, with 固 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3765.text: A conveyance for mountain travel. Formed from 木, with 纍 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “I used four conveyances”: boats on water, carts on land, 欙 in mountains and 䡅 in marshes.

shuowen:3766.text: A timber laid across water for crossing. Formed from 木, with 隺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3767.text: A bridge over water. Formed from 木, with 喬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3768.text: A bridge over water. Formed from 木 and 水, with 刅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3769.text: A general name for boats. Formed from 木, with 叜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3770.text: A large seagoing ship. Formed from 木, with 發 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3771.text: A boat’s oar. Formed from 木, with 咠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3772.text: A name for a large river boat. Formed from 木, with 蠡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3773.text: Wooden restraints for prisoners. Formed from 木, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3774.text: A lookout tower for guarding vegetation in marshes. Formed from 木, with 巢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3775.text: To pluck and take. Formed from 木 and 爪.

shuowen:3776.text: Wood shavings and rough slips shaved from timber. Formed from 木, with 巿 indicating the sound. Chen and Chu call a 櫝 杮.

shuowen:3777.text: A crosswise timber or barrier. Formed from 木, with 黃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3778.text: A clamp or restraining frame. Formed from 木, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3779.text: To fill. Formed from 木, with 光 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3780.text: To pound something with wood. Formed from 木, with 雋 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Yue defeated Wu at Zuili, 檇李.”

shuowen:3781.text: To strike. Formed from 木, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3782.text: To strike against. Formed from 木, with 丁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3783.text: An edge or ridge. Formed from 木, with 瓜 indicating the sound. Also: 柧棱, the highest part of a palace hall.

shuowen:3784.text: An edge or ridge, 柧. Formed from 木, with 夌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3785.text: What remains after a tree is felled. Formed from 木, with 獻 indicating the sound. The Book of Shang says: “Like a fallen tree having 纫𣡌”; the phrase describing remaining shoots or roots is uncertain.

shuowen:3786.text: Level. Formed from 木 and 平; 平 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:3787.text: Broken wood. Formed from 木, with 立 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3788.text: To chop obliquely. Formed from 木, with 差 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The mountains are not cut over.”

shuowen:3789.text: To sever. Formed from 木, with 出 indicating the sound. Read like 貀 in the Erya’s “貀 has no forefeet.”

shuowen:3790.text: Severed wood. Formed from 木, with 𠷎 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “𣚑柮.”

shuowen:3791.text: To split wood. Another explanation: to break. Formed from 木 and 斤.

shuowen:3792.text: Firewood. Formed from 木, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3793.text: 㮯, unsplit firewood. Formed from 木, with 完 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3794.text: 梡 wood not yet split. Formed from 木, with 圂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3795.text: 楄部, squared timber. Formed from 木, with 扁 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Squared timber to support the body.”

shuowen:3796.text: To press and bind with wood. Formed from 木, with 畐 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “In summer fit them with horn-bars and crosspieces.”

shuowen:3797.text: A flat piece, 楄; 枼 means thin. Formed from 木, with 丗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3798.text: To pile up and burn with fire. Formed from 木 and 火, with 酉 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Pile up the firewood and burn it.” The Rites of Zhou says: “With piled burning offerings sacrifice to the Director of the Center and Director of Destinies.”

shuowen:3799.text: To rest and stop. Formed from 人 leaning against 木.

shuowen:3800.text: To reach an end. Formed from 木, with 恆 indicating the sound.
